blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jacob had run from home after he tricked his brother Esau. He traveled a long way east, to the land where his mother's family lived. At a well in the fields, he asked the shepherds if they knew a man named Laban. They did. And here came his daughter now.

verses.text: And while he yet spake with them, Rachel came with her father’s sheep: for she kept them.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother’s brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother’s brother.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He had come all that way alone, not knowing what he would find. Now he was standing in front of his own family. No wonder he wept.

verses.text: And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s brother, and that he was Rebekah’s son: and she ran and told her father.

blocks.text: Jacob stayed and worked for a month. Then his uncle spoke to him about wages.

verses.text: And Laban said unto Jacob, Because thou art my brother, shouldest thou therefore serve me for nought? tell me, what shall thy wages be?

verses.text: And Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.

verses.text: Leah was tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The Bible says Leah had tender eyes. No one is sure exactly what that meant. What is clear is that Jacob only had eyes for her younger sister.

verses.text: And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.

blocks.text: Seven years of work, and they felt like a few days. That is how much he loved her.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When the seven years were over, Jacob asked for his bride, and Laban threw a wedding feast. But that night, Laban brought Leah instead of Rachel. In the dark, and under the veil, Jacob did not know.

verses.text: And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve with thee for Rachel? wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jacob had once fooled his own father in the dark by pretending to be his older brother. Now he was the one who had been fooled, by a father swapping the younger for the older.

verses.text: And Laban said, It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn.

verses.text: And he went in also unto Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him yet seven other years.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: It is not a happy story. Jacob was tricked. Rachel was kept waiting. And Leah was given to a man who did not want her, and she knew it.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: But the very next verse says that the LORD saw that Leah was not loved. He saw her. Leah's sons became fathers of tribes in Israel. One of them was Judah, and from Judah's family came King David, and in time, Jesus. The sister nobody chose was never overlooked by God.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to Gen 29:9-30; tagged sexual implied (v23 left out of the verses, the swap told in one plain sentence); Leah seen by God is v31, Judah to David to Jesus is the genealogy (Ruth 4, Matt 1), stated without references; 'tender eyed' left uncertain as it is.

cultural.note: Leah treated with tenderness, never as a joke about looks; the hurt of all three told honestly; no romance gloss on Laban's trick.
